title: Look Again: How We Check
subtitle: The Garden Welcome Sign
author: Maria Smith
visual_contract: Words and reveal labels appear above recognisable illustrations. The four sign positions use named corner symbols as well as location. Challenge pages do not contain their answers. Optional picture codes alone may be hidden inside scenes and never gate learning.
mission: Rebuild and check the four-picture Garden Welcome Sign so the garden gate can open before the morning visitors arrive.

new_guest.name: Ivo
new_guest.description: A friendly moss-green garden checker with a round magnifying lens and a checkerboard satchel.

pages.alt: Mia, Tavi and Sol wait beside the closed garden gate just after their turning-light adventure.

pages.text:
Last time, Mia, Sol and Tavi repaired the turning-light trail. The light reached the Sunrise Arch.

At the garden gate, Tavi asked, "How can we check our work?"
pages.subtext: Now the friends will learn how looking again can help them answer that question.
pages.alt: The repaired blue-moon and gold-sun trail glows behind Mia, Tavi and Sol. The garden gate ahead is still closed.

pages.badge: A SIGN FOR THE MORNING VISITORS
pages.text:
A board beside the gate showed four empty spaces. A card above it showed the pictures that belonged there.

The gate would open only after the friends rebuilt the Garden Welcome Sign and checked it carefully.
pages.subtext: Your mission: rebuild and check the sign before the morning visitors arrive.
pages.alt: A labelled picture plan shows a sunflower at the sun corner, a bee at the moon corner, a watering can at the leaf corner and a boot at the star corner. A second wooden sign has four empty spaces.

pages.text:
A small moss-green friend hurried out from the garden. He carried a round magnifying lens and a checkerboard satchel.

"Hello! I am Ivo, the garden checker. I can help you look again, but I will not choose your answers for you."
pages.subtext: Ivo is the one new friend on this adventure. The same four friends will solve one sign problem together.
pages.alt: Ivo, a friendly moss-green garden checker, greets Mia, Tavi and Sol. His round magnifying lens and checkerboard satchel are clearly labelled.

pages.text:
Ivo stood the picture plan where everyone could see it. Each space had a corner mark and one clear picture.

"First, let us say what we can see," said Mia.
pages.subtext: When you look at something that is shown and tell what you see, you make an observation. A guess is an answer chosen without checking what is shown.
pages.alt: The upright source plan has four labelled spaces. Sunflower is at the sun corner, bee at the moon corner, watering can at the leaf corner and boot at the star corner.

pages.text:
Look at the shown picture plan.

Which picture is in the MOON corner? Point to it before you turn the page.
pages.subtext: Use the picture that is really there. You do not need to guess.
pages.alt: The full upright plan stays visible. Four separate answer pictures show a sunflower, a bee, a watering can and a boot.

pages.badge: THE BEE IS IN THE MOON CORNER
pages.text:
The BEE is in the MOON corner. We know because we looked at the shown plan.

An OBSERVATION tells what we can see. A GUESS chooses without that check.
pages.subtext: Looking first gives the team a clear starting record. Find the optional picture code.
pages.alt: The bee picture in the moon-marked corner is outlined and labelled OBSERVED: BEE. The optional code LOOKCLOSE is hidden on Ivo's lens case.

pages.text:
Ivo opened his satchel. Inside were four large picture cards and one blank wooden sign.

The source plan stayed upright. The friends could look from the plan to the blank sign as often as they needed.
pages.subtext: The team will build from the shown source instead of choosing a favourite arrangement.
pages.alt: A source plan stands above a blank four-space sign. Four separate, labelled cards show a sunflower, bee, watering can and boot.

pages.badge: TRY IT - BUILD FROM THE PLAN
pages.text:
Point to each card, then point to its matching marked corner on the blank sign.

Use every card once. Leave no space empty.
pages.subtext: Check the source plan after every picture you place.
pages.alt: The four loose picture cards wait beside a blank sign with sun, moon, leaf and star corner marks. The source plan remains visible above them.

pages.text:
SUNFLOWER is in the SUN corner. BEE is in the MOON corner. WATERING CAN is in the LEAF corner. BOOT is in the STAR corner.

All four source pictures are on the sign, in the shown places.
pages.subtext: The team built one complete sign while the source was visible. Find the optional picture code.
pages.alt: The built sign matches the source plan. Every recognisable picture has its name above it and its corner symbol beside it. The optional code SIGNMAKER is hidden on the sign frame.

pages.text:
Ivo covered the source plan and the first sign with a leafy curtain. He put out a fresh blank sign and four fresh picture cards.

"Now we can try to rebuild what we remember," said Tavi.
pages.subtext: The covered sign has not vanished. It is still behind the curtain, ready for a later check.
pages.alt: A leafy curtain clearly covers the source plan and first sign. A second blank sign and four fresh picture cards wait in front.

pages.text:
Sol made this memory rebuild:

SUNFLOWER at SUN. BOOT at MOON. WATERING CAN at LEAF. BEE at STAR.

Does it match the covered source? Say MATCH or NOT SURE before the curtain opens.
pages.subtext: It is honest to say NOT SURE when the source is covered. The next page will let us check.
pages.alt: Sol's visible memory sign shows sunflower at sun, boot at moon, watering can at leaf and bee at star. The source is still covered, so no answer is exposed.

pages.text:
Ivo opened the curtain. The memory rebuild did NOT match the source. BEE and BOOT had traded places.

The friends did not hide Sol's try. They moved it onto a stand marked FIRST REBUILD.
pages.subtext: A failed attempt can help us check what changed. Find the optional picture code.
pages.alt: The uncovered source and Sol's first rebuild stand side by side. The source has bee at moon and boot at star. The first rebuild has boot at moon and bee at star. The optional code KEEPFIRST is hidden on the saved-try stand.

pages.text:
Look from the SOURCE sign to the FIRST REBUILD. Check one marked corner at a time.

Which two pictures are in different places?
pages.subtext: Point to the changed pictures on the first rebuild before you turn the page.
pages.alt: The source and first rebuild remain side by side with all four named pictures visible. No changed picture is circled yet.

pages.text:
BEE and BOOT are the two differences. SUNFLOWER and WATERING CAN stayed in their source places.

The friends compared every corner. They did not guess from one quick look.
pages.subtext: COMPARE means look at two records together to find what is the same and what is different. Find the optional picture code.
pages.alt: Bee and boot are circled on the first rebuild. Sunflower and watering can are labelled SAME. The source and failed attempt both remain visible.

pages.text:
Ivo had clipped one step card to a string after every picture Sol placed. The cards kept the order of his work.

"This step trace can show us what happened first, next and last," said Ivo.
pages.subtext: A TRACE is a kept record of the steps in the order they happened.
pages.alt: Four large step cards hang in order. Step 1 shows sunflower to sun. Step 2 shows watering can to leaf. Step 3 shows boot to moon. Step 4 shows bee to star.

pages.badge: TRY IT - FIND THE FIRST CHANGED STEP
pages.text:
Start at STEP 1. Compare each step card with the source plan.

Which is the first step that does not follow the source?
pages.subtext: Follow the record in order. Keep every step visible.
pages.alt: The source plan and all four ordered step cards are visible. None is marked as the answer.

pages.text:
STEP 3 put BOOT in the MOON corner. The source needed BEE there. STEP 4 then put BEE in the only space left.

The trace showed where the swap began.
pages.subtext: Keeping the ordered steps helps the team repair the cause, not just notice the final difference. Find the optional picture code.
pages.alt: Step 3 is outlined and labelled FIRST CHANGE. It shows boot moving to the moon corner while the source plan shows bee there. All four step cards remain visible.

pages.text:
The friends repaired the two changed places. The pictures now matched the source, but the wooden sign still had to fit between two gate hooks.

Ivo chose a ribbon labelled WIDTH. "This tool answers one question: Is the sign narrow enough to fit between the hooks?"
pages.subtext: WIDTH means the distance from one side to the other side. The ribbon is not checking the pictures or the height.
pages.alt: A clearly labelled WIDTH ribbon stretches from the left edge to the right edge of the repaired sign. Two green marks show the space between the gate hooks.

pages.text:
The sign's two side edges reach the two green marks on the WIDTH ribbon. The marks show the space between the hooks.

Does this width fit? Point to FITS or TOO WIDE.
pages.subtext: Answer only the width question that the tool was chosen to check.
pages.alt: The sign's left and right edges align with the two green width marks. Separate answer cards say FITS and TOO WIDE.

pages.text:
The WIDTH fits between the hooks. The two side edges meet the two green marks.

The ribbon answered its width question. It did NOT tell us whether the pictures match or whether the height fits.
pages.subtext: A measuring tool answers only the question we chose and declared. Find the optional picture code.
labels: PICTURES: NOT CHECKED BY THIS RIBBON
pages.alt: The width edges and green marks are labelled FITS. Separate labels clearly state that this ribbon did not check picture positions or height.

pages.text:
The trio turned their repaired sign away. Ivo took a fresh blank board, fresh picture cards and the original source plan behind the hedge.

He rebuilt the sign without seeing their answer.
pages.subtext: An INDEPENDENT CHECK uses its own clear path instead of copying the first answer.
pages.alt: A hedge separates the covered team sign from Ivo's fresh check board. Ivo can see the original source plan but cannot see the team's answer.

pages.badge: TRY IT - COMPARE THE TWO CHECKS
pages.text:
Now uncover the TEAM SIGN and IVO'S CHECK. Compare one marked corner at a time.

Do all four picture places match? Point to CONFIRM or DISAGREE.
pages.subtext: Confirm means the independent check agrees. Disagree means the two results do not match.
pages.alt: The team's repaired sign and Ivo's separately rebuilt check sign are visible side by side. Each shows sunflower at sun, bee at moon, watering can at leaf and boot at star.

pages.text:
All four picture places match. Ivo's fresh check CONFIRMS the team's repaired sign.

A friend check can confirm, disagree, or show that more work is needed.
pages.subtext: This check confirms the picture places. It does not erase the failed first rebuild. Find the optional picture code.
pages.alt: Four connecting marks pair the same pictures on the team sign and Ivo's check sign. The failed first rebuild remains on its stand nearby.

pages.text:
"The width fits, so the whole sign must fit," said Mia.

"I disagree," said Ivo. "The width ribbon did not check the height."

What should the team do next: guess, vote, or check the HEIGHT with a height tool?
pages.subtext: A disagreement does not make the loudest person the answer. It can show that more work is needed.
pages.alt: Mia points to the width record. Ivo points to the unchecked top and bottom edges. Three answer cards show GUESS, VOTE and CHECK HEIGHT.

pages.text:
The team chose a HEIGHT ribbon and declared a new question: Is the sign short enough for the gate?

The top and bottom edges reached the green height marks. HEIGHT fits too.
pages.subtext: Ivo did not prove Mia wrong by saying so. Their disagreement showed which question still needed checking. Find the optional picture code.
pages.alt: A vertical HEIGHT ribbon runs from the bottom edge to the top edge of the sign. Both edges align with green height marks and are labelled HEIGHT: FITS.

pages.text:
Only the final checkpoint remained. The gate showed four questions:

Do the pictures match the source? Does the width fit? Does the height fit? Did a separate friend check agree?
pages.subtext: The gate will open only when every declared check has a visible record.
pages.alt: The repaired sign stands beside four large checkpoint spaces. The source comparison, width record, height record and Ivo's separate check are all visible.

pages.badge: TRY IT - MATCH EACH CHECK TO ITS RECORD
pages.text:
Match each gate question to the record that answers it.

Point to PICTURES, WIDTH, HEIGHT and FRIEND CHECK in turn. Can every question be supported?
pages.subtext: Use the visible records. Do not add a tick just because the sign looks nice.
pages.alt: Four named gate questions and four separate record cards wait to be matched. No checkpoint tick is filled yet.

pages.text:
PICTURES match the source. WIDTH fits. HEIGHT fits. IVO'S FRESH CHECK agrees.

The checked rebuild passed every declared checkpoint. The gate opened before the visitors arrived!
pages.subtext: The first failed rebuild and the width-only conclusion stay in the checking book. Find the optional picture code.
pages.alt: All four checkpoint spaces show supported ticks beside their records. The garden gate stands open behind the checked sign. The saved first rebuild remains in Ivo's checking book.

pages.text:
You looked at what was shown instead of guessing. You built the sign, covered it, rebuilt it, and kept the first try when it did not match. You followed the step trace, used each measuring tool for its own question, and asked Ivo to check by a fresh path.

A check can CONFIRM, DISAGREE, or show that MORE WORK is needed.
pages.subtext: This matters because looking again helps us say what we observed, find what changed, and know which question still needs an answer.
pages.alt: Five labelled pictures recap the child's actions: looking at the source, saving the failed rebuild, following the step cards, measuring width and height separately, and comparing Ivo's fresh check.

pages.text:
The morning visitors followed the checked sign into the garden. Mia, Sol, Tavi and Ivo watched each visitor find the right path.

At the far wall, another Star Door gave one soft click. The friends smiled. They would discover where it led on their next learning adventure.
pages.subtext: End of the Early Years checking adventure. The next book remains a new question until its own reviewed syllabus is opened.
pages.alt: The checked four-picture sign guides visitors through the open garden gate. Mia, Tavi, Sol and Ivo look towards a closed Star Door at the far garden wall.
